author: Seung Wook
problem: Read an 8-character string with one K, one Q, two R, two B and two N. Print Yes if the two B's are at positions of different parity and the K is between the two R's; otherwise print No.
bug_description: Operator precedence: firstB+secondB % 2 computes firstB + (secondB % 2), so B's on the same parity are accepted unless the first B is at index 0.

comments.accurate: Checks the Chess960 rules: bishops on opposite-coloured squares and the king between the rooks
comments.wrong_behavior: Checks the king is between the rooks; a bishop pair is rejected only when the first bishop starts the row and the second sits on an even index
comments.wrong_location: Bishop parity check verified; check the rook split, which assumes the first R comes before the K
